summary: Food and eating. Buddhist texts count four kinds of food, of which morsels are only the first.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Newton–Leipnik trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 魂 takes the highest of the eight points and 魄 the lowest, after the Liji’s 魂氣歸于天，形魄歸于地. A design choice, not a claim.

satellites.title: The Four Foods
satellites.evidence: The Abhidharmakośa counts four foods that sustain beings: 段食, food in morsels; 觸食, contact; 思食, volition; and 識食, consciousness. It cites the Buddha that 四食皆為病癰箭根 — all four are disease, boil and arrow, roots of aging and death.

checked.note: 世尊說四食皆為病癰箭根…觸食…思食…識食

satellites.title: Food and Sex Are Nature
satellites.evidence: Mencius 6A4: Gaozi says 食色，性也 — appetite for food and sex is human nature — and that humaneness is inside us while rightness is outside. Mencius rejects the second claim.
satellites.caveat: The famous line is Gaozi’s, Mencius’s opponent, not Mencius’s own view.
